In the US Market, I think that the change is cyclical and ties to the political cycle. Seriously. Big changes come in increments of four years.

 

So one tries to predict whom will win the next election and whether the markets will see them as good or bad. IMHO most of the time it's obvious, the markets wanted Hillary to win.

 

So mentally you can make a trend line between the current stock prices and what you think that prices will be after the next election. If that trend line is sloping up, anyone that agrees with you will be bullish on the market.

 

To me that's how you spot corrections - if stock prices get too far off of the imaginary trend line, then the market needs to react. People can put it off for a while, but you want it to happen.

 

To that I'll add that with practice you can predict how many "beats" are going to happen during the interval. Like I'm predicting one or two beats between now and the election. If you wanted to count that little bump we just hit as the correction, then the stocks will dip one more time before the election.

 

But if you don't think that's the correction, we're due for one more. Have a contingency plan for that.
